name: Sprocket
text: Adopt staged rollout for prompt changes. This lets us test tweaks on a small slice of traffic before full deployment, catching errors early without risking the whole system. The trade-off is slower iteration speed for fewer outages.

name: Gauge
text: Staged rollout misses 20% of reworded prompts—enough to let bad variants slip through. Better: A/B test with *prompt hashing* to detect reworded variants before they hit traffic. Settle it by running a week-long A/B test comparing staged rollout vs. hashing on a 1% traffic slice, measuring error rates and iteration speed.

name: Sprocket
text:
Do A/B test prompt hashing on 1% traffic for one week. Hashing catches reworded prompts early by comparing semantic fingerprints, cutting error rate by ~20% compared to staged rollout. Trade-off: slower prompt iteration while we wait for hash results, but we avoid costly outages from bad variants slipping through.

name: Gauge
text: Hashing won’t catch semantic drift—only exact rewordings. The real risk is mistaking noise for signal: a hash collision or a prompt tweak that changes meaning but keeps the same hash could let bad variants through while slowing iteration. Settle it by running a week-long A/B test comparing staged rollout vs. staged rollout *plus* human review of the 20% flagged reworded prompts—measure error rate and iteration speed.

name: Ratchet
text: DECISION: Run a week-long A/B test on 1% traffic comparing staged rollout vs. prompt hashing, measuring error rates and semantic drift—Gauge owns the test design, metrics, and call.
